# Rotated shapes with empty Wordprocessing text boxes

Original XML generated by `tools/rotated_empty_text_fixture.py`, using the
repository's original shape-theme package and shape construction helpers.
No corpus artwork or third-party document engine is included.

Each of four rows pairs the same blue custom geometry without a text box and
with one empty paragraph. Rotations are 0, 30, 21398351/60000 and 90 degrees.
The final empty box also declares upright=true. The reference application opened
the source read-only and exported the one-page PDF. Both shapes in each pair
have the same visible geometry. The native PNG is rasterized at 96 DPI;
`hashes.json` binds the DOCX, PDF and PNG. The source passes four XML checks.

This is ordinary DrawingML rotation (ECMA-376 Part 1 §20.1.7.6 xfrm) with
WordprocessingShape text boxes (MS-ODRAWXML wps:txbx/wps:bodyPr). An empty box
contains no glyphs to orient; this fixture establishes no new reference/spec
divergence. The reader validates the complete text box and retains its paragraph
metrics/source XML. Actual text or fields on rotated shapes remain guarded.

Unit tests cover retained geometry and empty paragraphs through editing/export,
exact no-edit/undo preservation, and rejection of malformed or nonempty boxes.
Browser coverage compares native blue masks in both directions within one pixel,
and repeats after editing and reopening. No claim of general rotated-text
support is made.
